summary: Embedding provenance header flip leads to candidate index shift and sporadic rerank tail latency
description: Customer reports that after a recent edge proxy rollout they observed (a) top-k candidate reordering for the same queries compared to prior baseline and (b) intermittent 200–800ms tail latency spikes from the rerank endpoint. Early signs point to an intermittent header that indicates embedding provenance being flipped/omitted between the embedding ingestion pipeline and the reranker, causing a fallback normalization path and extra serialization that both changes candidate ordering and increases tail latency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends batch of 64 documents to /embeddings with header X-Embed-Provenance: origin-v2 (consistent payloads).
2) Immediately call /rerank with the same feature IDs and request top_k=10 under high-concurrency (QPS ~120).
3) Observe that responses intermittently have different top-3 ordering than previous baseline recorded 24 hours earlier for identical payloads.
4) Observe per-request latency for rerank spikes on a subset of requests (200–800ms extra) correlated with proxy logs showing X-Embed-Provenance missing or set to origin-v1.
5) Replaying the same traffic through a staging proxy (pre-rollout) does not reproduce the issue consistently.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Initial triage by Support (Maya): Pattern of header toggling observed in proxy traces. Customer provided request/response pairs and golden baselines.

2026-03-10 - CS Eng (Ethan) reproduced topk variance in a controlled replay when intentionally toggling X-Embed-Provenance between v1 and v2; reranker uses a fast path when provenance==v2 that avoids an extra normalization/quant-decoder, producing deterministic ordering.

2026-03-11 - Deeper trace: a recent edge-proxy image (rev 2026.03.05) contains a batching/jitter optimization that coalesces requests; under certain race windows it strips or overwrites X-Embed-Provenance when upstream connection pooling forwards to an older backend instance.

2026-03-11 - Hypothesis: Coalescing + sticky connection to mixed-version pool occasionally drops provenance header, triggering reranker compatibility codepath which applies fp32 fallback normalization and additional serialization, both changing numeric values and adding 200–700ms latency.
2026-03-11 - Risk assessment: High — affects rerank determinism for dedicated customers with heterogeneous edge fleets; correlated with elevated tail latency reported by customer.

2026-03-12 - Temporary mitigation validated: Proxy config change to disable coalescing/jitter optimization for the customer's canary pool eliminated header flips in replays and restored baseline top-k and tail latency for 48k replays.

2026-03-12 - Engineering plan: roll back proxy optimization in affected pool, add strict header passthrough tests, and add guard in proxy to reject requests missing X-Embed-Provenance for embed/rerank flows (return 4xx) to avoid silent fallback.

resolution: Mitigation applied: disabled proxy coalescing in affected canary pool and customer confirmed restoration of baseline top-k order and reduced rerank tail latency. Long-term fix in progress: PR opened to ensure header passthrough across pooling logic and add unit/integration tests; proxy will return 4xx for missing X-Embed-Provenance on embed/rerank flows to force observable failure instead of silent fallback. Follow-ups: monitor for 72h post-rollout, add regression test to CI, and notify customers with guidance on how to surface provenance header on custom proxies.
